title: A+ Core 1 (220-1201) practice exam
note: Original questions written for MyNextCert from the public 220-1201 exam objectives. Not real exam questions.

q.q: A cutter's rugged tablet now rocks on a flat table, and the back cover has started to lift away from the frame. What should the technician do first?
o: Charge it overnight and see if it flattens
Charging a swollen battery adds heat and risk. It won't go back to normal.
Power it down and take the swollen battery out of service
Right. A lifting case means a swelling lithium-ion battery, which can catch fire. Stop using it, power it off and replace the battery, then recycle it properly.
Press the cover back down and seal it with tape
Pressing on a swollen battery can puncture it and start a fire.
Recalibrate the battery by fully draining it
Calibration fixes inaccurate charge readings. It can't shrink a battery that has swollen.

q.q: A laptop's touch screen shows a perfect image, but taps register in the wrong spot or not at all. Which part most likely needs replacing?
o: The digitizer
Right. The digitizer is the touch layer. A clear image with bad touch points to it, not the display panel.
The LCD display panel
The image is fine, so the panel that makes it is working.
The Wi-Fi antenna in the lid
The antenna affects wireless signal, not touch.
The display inverter
An inverter powers older CCFL backlights. A bad one makes the screen dim, not the touch input wrong.

q.q: A technician upgrades a user's laptop from 8 GB to 16 GB. The laptop uses DDR5. Which module should they order?
o: A DDR4 SODIMM
DDR4 and DDR5 are keyed differently and aren't compatible.
A DDR5 DIMM
Full-size DIMMs are for desktops and won't fit a laptop slot.
An M.2 NVMe module
M.2 NVMe is storage, not memory.
A DDR5 SODIMM
Right. Laptops use the smaller SODIMM form factor, and the generation must match the slot (DDR5).

q.q: A field laptop's storage must be upgraded for faster boot times. The motherboard has one M.2 slot keyed for NVMe. Which drive gives the biggest speed gain?
o: A 2.5-inch 7,200 RPM hard drive
A spinning drive is slower than any SSD, and there's no 2.5-inch bay here.
An M.2 SATA SSD
It may physically fit some slots, but it's limited to SATA speed, and an NVMe-only slot may not support it.
An mSATA SSD
mSATA is an older form factor that doesn't fit an M.2 slot.
An M.2 NVMe SSD
Right. NVMe drives connect over PCIe lanes, which are much faster than SATA.

q.q: Before replacing a laptop keyboard, which step protects both the technician and the laptop?
o: Spray the keyboard area with compressed air while it runs
Compressed air is fine for cleaning, but not as a safety step, and the laptop should be off.
Put the laptop on a carpeted floor so it can't slide around during the repair
Carpet builds static, which is the opposite of what you want.
Leave it powered on so the new keyboard is detected right away
Working on a powered laptop risks shorts and shock.
Unplug AC, disconnect the battery and wear an ESD strap
Right. Removing power sources prevents shorts, and ESD protection keeps static from damaging the board.

q.q: Staff want to tap their phones on a reader to badge in and pay at the exchange. Which technology does this use?
o: Bluetooth
Bluetooth works at about 10 m and needs pairing. It isn't used for tap-to-pay.
Wi-Fi Direct
Wi-Fi Direct links devices over longer distances for file sharing, not taps.
NFC
Right. Near-field communication works at a few centimeters and is used for tap-to-pay and badges.
Infrared
Infrared needs line of sight and isn't used for phone payments.

q.q: A user wants one cable from a laptop to a dock that carries video to two monitors, USB peripherals, Ethernet and charging power. Which connection fits best?
o: USB-C with Thunderbolt or DisplayPort Alt Mode
Right. USB-C with Thunderbolt or Alt Mode can carry video, data and power delivery together.
A USB 2.0 Type-A cable
USB 2.0 is too slow for two monitors and doesn't supply laptop charging power.
A VGA cable plus a powered USB 3.0 splitter hub
VGA is analog video only and can't carry power or data.
HDMI
HDMI carries video and audio only. It can't charge the laptop or carry USB devices.

q.q: A new Bluetooth headset won't connect to a phone. Bluetooth is on and the headset is charged. What should the technician check next?
o: Put the headset in pairing mode, then pair it
Right. Bluetooth devices must be paired before they connect, and many need a button held to enter pairing mode.
Turn on the phone's hotspot so the headset can join it
A hotspot shares the phone's internet connection. It doesn't pair accessories.
Turn on NFC on the phone
Some headsets use NFC to start pairing, but it isn't required. Bluetooth pairing still has to happen.
Connect the phone to Wi-Fi
Bluetooth works without Wi-Fi.

q.q: A deployed member's phone burns through its monthly data in a week because photos back up over cellular. Which setting change best fixes it?
o: Turn off Bluetooth
Bluetooth doesn't use cellular data.
Enable the phone's hotspot
A hotspot shares cellular data and uses more of it.
Limit photo sync to Wi-Fi only
Right. Restricting cloud sync to Wi-Fi keeps large uploads off the cellular data cap.
Turn on airplane mode during the duty day
That blocks calls and texts too, which is far more than needed.

q.q: A new phone must receive unit email, contacts and calendar, and IT must be able to wipe only the work data if it's lost. What should be set up?
o: Pair it with the user's laptop over Bluetooth
Bluetooth pairing doesn't set up mail or allow a remote wipe.
Enroll it in MDM and add the work account through it
Right. Mobile device management pushes the account settings and can remotely wipe the managed work data.
Turn on location services
Location helps find a lost phone, but it doesn't configure mail or wipe data.
Forward work email to a personal account
That breaks policy and IT can't control the data.

q.q: A phone shows full Wi-Fi bars on the base network but no internet. Other phones on the same network work. What should the technician try first?
o: Turn on Bluetooth tethering
Tethering is a workaround, not a fix for the Wi-Fi problem.
Replace the phone's battery and Wi-Fi antenna
Battery health doesn't cause this kind of problem.
Factory reset the phone
A reset erases everything and is a last resort.
Forget the network and reconnect
Right. Rejoining clears bad saved settings or a stale lease for that network.

q.q: Which setting lets a phone keep its cellular service working while making calls over Wi-Fi in a building with weak cell signal?
o: Wi-Fi calling
Right. Wi-Fi calling routes calls and texts over the Wi-Fi network when cell coverage is weak.
Data roaming
Roaming uses other carriers' cell networks. It doesn't use Wi-Fi.
Mobile hotspot
A hotspot shares the phone's own cellular connection.
Airplane mode
Airplane mode turns off the cellular radio.

q.q: A work phone needs a second cellular line for travel without a second physical SIM tray. Which feature supports this?
o: eSIM
Right. An eSIM is a built-in, programmable SIM, so a second carrier profile can be added without a physical card.
PRL update
A PRL update refreshes which towers a phone prefers on some older networks. It doesn't add a line.
NFC chip
NFC is for short-range taps like payments.
MicroSD
MicroSD adds storage, not a cellular line.

q.q: A technician is setting up a docking station for a laptop. Which TWO checks matter most before buying it? (Choose two.)
o: The dock has a VGA port for every monitor
VGA is old analog video. Modern monitors use HDMI or DisplayPort.
The laptop has a compatible port (such as Thunderbolt or USB-C with Alt Mode)
Right. Without a port that supports video and data, the dock can't drive monitors.
The dock's power delivery wattage meets the laptop's charging needs
Right. A dock that supplies less wattage than the laptop needs charges slowly or not at all.
The dock's color matches the laptop
Color has nothing to do with compatibility.
The dock supports NFC pairing
Docks connect by cable, not NFC.

q.q: A user can browse websites by IP address, but no names resolve. The firewall team says they recently tightened outbound rules. Which port is most likely blocked?
o: Port 80 is HTTP. Blocking it would also stop browsing by IP over HTTP.
Port 110 is POP3 mail.
Port 67 is DHCP. It assigns addresses; it doesn't resolve names.
Right. DNS turns names into IP addresses, and it uses port 53 (mostly UDP).

q.q: A help desk tech needs to take over a user's Windows desktop remotely with the built-in Microsoft tool. Which port must be open on the user's PC?
o: TCP 22
Port 22 is SSH, used for encrypted command-line sessions.
TCP 445
Port 445 is SMB file sharing.
TCP 3389
Right. Remote Desktop Protocol listens on TCP 3389.
TCP 23
Port 23 is Telnet, an old clear-text remote shell.

q.q: Which protocol is connectionless and doesn't guarantee delivery, which makes it a good fit for live voice and video?
o: IMAP
IMAP retrieves mail over TCP.
UDP
Right. UDP sends without a handshake or retransmission, so it has less delay. Late voice packets are useless anyway.
SMTP
SMTP is an application protocol for sending mail, and it runs over TCP.
TCP/IP
TCP is connection-oriented. It resends lost data, which adds delay.

q.q: A user wants email to stay on the server so they can see the same folders on their phone and laptop. Which protocol and port should the mail client use?
o: POP3 on 110
POP3 usually downloads mail and removes it from the server, so devices get out of sync.
SMTP on 25
SMTP sends mail. It doesn't retrieve it.
IMAP on 143 (or 993 with TLS)
Right. IMAP keeps messages and folders on the server and syncs them across devices.
FTP on 21
FTP transfers files, not email.

q.q: A new office needs Wi-Fi that can use the 6 GHz band for less crowded channels. Which standard should the access points support?
o: 802.11ac uses only 5 GHz.
Wi-Fi 6E (802.11ax)
Right. Wi-Fi 6E extends 802.11ax into the 6 GHz band.
802.11n uses 2.4 and 5 GHz, not 6 GHz.
802.11b/g/n tri-mode
Those use 2.4 GHz (n also 5 GHz). None use 6 GHz.

q.q: A warehouse wants to track pallets by reading tags from a few meters away without line of sight. Which technology fits?
o: Bluetooth pairing
Pairing every pallet tag would be impractical, and the tags would need power.
Infrared
Infrared needs line of sight.
RFID
Right. RFID readers can power and read passive tags from a distance, without seeing them.
NFC tags
NFC only works within a few centimeters.

q.q: Users at the far end of a building get a strong 2.4 GHz signal but a weak 5 GHz signal from the same AP. Why?
o: 5 GHz is only for mobile phones
Laptops and many other devices use 5 GHz.
Higher frequencies have shorter range and weaker wall penetration
Right. 5 GHz has more bandwidth but shorter range and weaker wall penetration than 2.4 GHz.
5 GHz requires WPA3
Security settings don't change signal range.
The AP limits 5 GHz to one user
APs serve many clients on 5 GHz.

q.q: A unit wants one appliance at the internet edge that combines firewall, IPS, antivirus and web filtering. What is this called?
o: A proxy server
A proxy can filter web traffic, but it doesn't bundle firewall and IPS.
A spam gateway that scans all mail
A spam gateway only filters email.
A UTM appliance
Right. A UTM appliance bundles several security functions in one box.
A load balancer
A load balancer spreads traffic across servers.

q.q: All switches, routers and servers must send their event logs to one central server for review. Which service is that server running?
o: NetFlow
NetFlow records traffic flows between hosts, not device event logs.
AAA
AAA handles authentication, authorization and accounting, not general log collection.
Syslog
Right. A syslog server collects log messages sent by many devices.
DHCP
DHCP hands out IP addresses.

q.q: A water treatment plant near a base uses old control systems to run pumps and valves. Which term describes these systems?
o: A SAN
A SAN is network storage.
Consumer IoT smart home hubs
Smart speakers are consumer IoT devices, not plant controls.
A UTM
A UTM is a security appliance.
SCADA (industrial control)
Right. Supervisory control and data acquisition systems monitor and control industrial equipment.

q.q: Outside mail servers are rejecting the unit's email as possible spoofing. Which DNS record lists the servers allowed to send mail for the domain?
o: A TXT record (SPF)
Right. SPF is published as a TXT record and tells receivers which servers may send for the domain.
An AAAA record
AAAA maps a name to an IPv6 address.
A CNAME record
A CNAME makes one name an alias of another.
An MX record for the mail server
MX says where mail for the domain should be delivered. It doesn't list allowed senders.

q.q: A label printer must always keep the same IP address, but the team still wants DHCP to manage it. What should they set up?
o: A DHCP reservation
Right. A reservation ties an IP to the printer's MAC address, so it always gets the same address from DHCP.
A shorter lease time
Shorter leases make address changes more likely, not less.
A second DHCP scope
Another scope adds more addresses. It doesn't pin one device.
A DHCP exclusion range
An exclusion stops DHCP from giving out the address at all.

q.q: Which DNS record maps a host name to an IPv4 address?
o: A
Right. An A record holds the IPv4 address for a name.
MX
MX names the mail server for a domain.
PTR
PTR maps an IP address back to a name.
AAAA
AAAA holds an IPv6 address.

q.q: A unit wants staff, guest and camera traffic kept apart on the same physical switches. What should be configured?
o: VLANs
Right. VLANs split one physical switch into separate logical networks.
A VPN
A VPN encrypts traffic between sites or users. It doesn't split a local switch.
A DHCP reservation
Reservations fix IP addresses. They don't separate traffic.
DNS
DNS resolves names.

q.q: A ceiling access point needs power, but there's no outlet nearby and the switch doesn't supply PoE. What is the simplest fix?
o: Use a hub instead of the switch
Hubs don't supply power and are obsolete.
Replace the cable with Cat 6a
A better cable doesn't add power.
Add a patch panel and a longer patch cable
A patch panel organizes cable runs. It doesn't supply power.
Add a PoE injector between switch and AP
Right. A PoE injector adds power to the Ethernet cable going to the AP.

q.q: Which device connects a home or small office to a fiber provider and converts the optical signal for the router?
o: A DSL modem
A DSL modem works on telephone lines.
An ONT (optical network terminal)
Right. The ONT is the provider's fiber endpoint. It hands off Ethernet to the router.
A PoE injector
A PoE injector adds power to Ethernet.
A cable modem
A cable modem works on coaxial cable service.

q.q: A small office needs a switch where the IT staff can set up VLANs and see port statistics. Which type should they buy?
o: An unmanaged switch
Unmanaged switches work out of the box but can't be configured.
A hub
A hub repeats traffic out every port and can't do VLANs.
A repeater
A repeater only extends a signal.
A managed switch
Right. Managed switches can be configured with VLANs, monitoring and other features.

q.q: A new SOHO wireless router arrives for a recruiting office. Which change is the most important first step?
o: Turn the transmit power to maximum
More power can spread the signal outside the office and doesn't secure anything.
Change the SSID to the office's name
That's fine, but it does little for security, and it advertises who owns the network.
Turn on WPS for easy device setup
WPS has known weaknesses. It should usually be off.
Change the default admin password
Right. Default router credentials are published online and are among the first things attackers try.

q.q: A recruiter's home office needs a camera server reachable from the internet on TCP 8443. What should be set on the SOHO router?
o: A DMZ host for every device
A DMZ host exposes all ports of a device. Doing it for everything is dangerous.
A static IP on the router's LAN side only
That alone doesn't let outside traffic reach the camera.
Content filtering that allows the camera site
Content filtering blocks outbound web categories. It doesn't let traffic in.
Port forwarding of TCP 8443 to the camera server
Right. Port forwarding sends inbound traffic on one port to a specific internal host.

q.q: Which security setting should a SOHO Wi-Fi network use if all its devices support it?
o: WPA with TKIP
WPA/TKIP is outdated and weak.
WPA3
Right. WPA3 is the current standard and resists offline password guessing better than WPA2.
WEP-128
WEP is broken and can be cracked in minutes.
Open with MAC filtering
MAC filtering is easy to spoof, and open networks aren't encrypted.

q.q: A PC on a SOHO network has 192.168.1.50/24, gateway 192.168.1.1. Which change would break its internet access but keep local file sharing working?
o: Setting the gateway to 192.168.2.1
Right. The gateway must be on the local subnet. Local traffic still works, but internet-bound traffic has nowhere to go.
Changing the hostname
The hostname doesn't affect routing.
Setting DNS to the public resolver 8.8.8.8
Changing DNS to a working public server doesn't break internet access.
Renewing the DHCP lease
Renewing keeps or refreshes the same settings.

q.q: A remote lighthouse station has no cable, DSL or fiber. Video calls work but have a long delay every time someone speaks. Which connection is it most likely using?
o: A wired LAN
A LAN is local. It doesn't connect the site to the internet.
Fiber
Fiber has very low latency.
Geostationary satellite
Right. Signals travel about 36,000 km up and back, which adds a lot of latency.
Cable
Cable broadband has low latency and isn't at this site.

q.q: A user connects a wireless headset, a smartwatch and a phone within a few meters of their desk. Which network type is this?
o: MAN
A MAN covers a city or campus.
LAN
A LAN covers a building or office.
WAN
A WAN spans large distances between sites.
PAN
Right. A personal area network covers a few meters around one person.

q.q: Several buildings across a city are linked into one network owned by the city government. Which network type is this?
o: MAN
Right. A metropolitan area network covers a city or a large campus.
WLAN
A WLAN is a wireless LAN within a building.
SAN
A SAN is a dedicated storage network.
PAN
A PAN covers a few meters.

q.q: A technician has to terminate new Cat 6 runs onto a patch panel in the closet. Which tool do they need?
o: A Wi-Fi analyzer
A Wi-Fi analyzer measures wireless signals.
A crimper
A crimper attaches RJ45 plugs to cable ends, not wires to a panel.
A punchdown tool
Right. A punchdown tool seats each wire into the panel's IDC terminals and trims the excess.
A loopback plug
A loopback plug tests a port.

q.q: A technician needs to find which of 48 unlabeled cables in the closet runs to Office 214. Which tool fits?
o: A crimper
A crimper makes cable ends.
A multimeter
A multimeter measures voltage, resistance and current.
A cable stripper
A stripper removes cable jacket.
A toner probe
Right. A toner puts a tone on the cable at the office jack, and the probe finds that tone in the closet.

q.q: A technician wants to test whether a NIC port can send and receive at all, with no network attached. Which tool should they use?
o: A loopback plug
Right. A loopback plug routes the port's transmit pins back to its receive pins.
A Wi-Fi analyzer
A Wi-Fi analyzer measures wireless signals.
A toner and probe kit
A toner traces cables.
A punchdown tool
A punchdown tool terminates wires on panels.

q.q: A watch center wants monitors with deep blacks and very high contrast for night operations, and accepts some risk of burn-in. Which panel type fits?
o: CCFL-backlit LCD
CCFL backlights are old technology with weaker contrast.
OLED
Right. Each OLED pixel makes its own light and can turn fully off, which gives true blacks. Static images can burn in.
TN LCD
TN panels are fast and cheap, but they have weak contrast and narrow viewing angles.
IPS LCD
IPS has good color and angles, but a backlight keeps its blacks from being truly black.

q.q: A graphic designer needs accurate color and wide viewing angles. Which LCD panel type is the best fit?
o: IPS
Right. In-plane switching panels have the best color accuracy and viewing angles of the common LCD types.
CRT
CRTs are obsolete.
TN
TN is fast, but colors shift when viewed off-angle.
VA
VA has strong contrast, but color and angles are usually behind IPS.

q.q: A gamer's new monitor supports 144 Hz, but motion still looks like 60 Hz. The cable is HDMI 1.4. What is the most likely cause?
o: The panel's color gamut is too small
Color gamut doesn't limit refresh rate.
The monitor is set to portrait mode in the OS settings
Orientation doesn't change refresh rate.
The HDMI 1.4 link lacks bandwidth for 144 Hz
Right. Older HDMI versions have limited bandwidth. A DisplayPort or newer HDMI cable and port may be needed.
The monitor needs an inverter
Inverters power old CCFL backlights.

q.q: Network cable that runs through a drop ceiling used as an air return must meet fire code. Which jacket is required?
o: Plenum-rated
Right. Plenum cable resists fire and gives off less toxic smoke in air-handling spaces.
PVC (riser-rated)
Riser cable is for vertical shafts between floors, not plenum spaces.
Shielded twisted pair
Shielding reduces interference, but it isn't a fire rating.
Direct burial
Direct burial cable is for underground runs.

q.q: A technician must make a straight-through patch cable to match the T568B jacks in a building. Which wire goes on pin 1?
o: White/green, then green
White/green is pin 1 in T568A.
White/orange
Right. T568B order starts with white/orange, orange, white/green, blue.
Blue
Blue is pin 4 in both standards.
Orange
Solid orange is pin 2 in T568B.

q.q: Which internal connector supplies power to a modern SATA SSD?
o: A 6-pin PCIe auxiliary power cable
PCIe power connectors feed graphics cards.
A 4-pin Molex
Molex powered older IDE drives and fans. SATA drives need SATA power.
A 24-pin ATX
The 24-pin connector powers the motherboard.
A 15-pin SATA power connector
Right. SATA drives use a 15-pin power connector and a separate 7-pin data connector.

q.q: A technician must connect an older projector with only a VGA input to a laptop with only HDMI out. What do they need?
o: A USB 2.0 cable
USB 2.0 doesn't carry the video signal to a VGA port.
An active HDMI-to-VGA converter
Right. HDMI is digital and VGA is analog, so the signal must be converted, not just adapted.
A passive HDMI-to-VGA adapter cable
A passive cable can't convert a digital signal to analog.
A DVI-D cable
DVI-D is digital only, so it doesn't fix the VGA problem.

q.q: Which connector is used for cable TV and cable modem service?
o: F-type on RG-6 coax
Right. Cable providers use RG-6 coaxial cable with screw-on F-type connectors.
LC on fiber
LC is a fiber connector.
RJ45 on Cat 6
RJ45 is for Ethernet.
RJ11 on twisted pair
RJ11 is for phone lines and DSL.

q.q: A server for a sector's records system must detect and correct single-bit memory errors on its own. Which RAM feature is needed?
o: Dual-channel
Dual-channel increases bandwidth. It doesn't correct errors.
Virtual RAM
Virtual memory uses disk space when RAM runs low. It doesn't correct errors.
ECC
Right. Error-correcting code memory detects and fixes single-bit errors, which matters for servers.
SODIMM
SODIMM is a smaller form factor for laptops.

q.q: A desktop has two RAM slots in dual-channel mode. The user has one 16 GB stick. Which upgrade gives the best memory performance?
o: Add an ECC stick next to the non-ECC one
Mixing ECC and non-ECC usually isn't supported.
Turn up the size of virtual memory
Paging to disk is much slower than real RAM.
Two matched 8 GB or 16 GB sticks in the paired slots
Right. Dual-channel needs a matching pair in the right slots to double the memory bandwidth.
One 32 GB stick in the same slot
A single stick still runs in single-channel mode.

q.q: Which statement about DDR4 and DDR5 is correct?
o: DDR4 is faster than DDR5
DDR5 is the newer, faster generation.
They're keyed differently and aren't interchangeable
Right. Each generation is keyed differently to stop it from being installed in the wrong slot.
DDR5 works in DDR4 slots, just at the lower DDR4 speed
They aren't backward compatible at all.
They use the same voltage and pins
Their voltage and pin layout differ.

q.q: A file server needs to survive any single drive failure while giving as much usable space as possible from four drives. Which RAID level fits?
o: RAID 10
RAID 10 survives failures but uses half the total space for mirrors.
RAID 5
Right. RAID 5 stripes data with parity across 3+ drives, survives one failure, and uses about one drive's worth of space for parity.
RAID 1
RAID 1 mirrors two drives, so half the space goes to the copy.
RAID 0
RAID 0 has no redundancy. One failed drive loses everything.

q.q: A database server must keep running even if two drives fail at the same time. Which RAID level guarantees that?
o: RAID 1
A two-drive mirror survives one failure.
RAID 5
RAID 5 survives only one drive failure.
RAID 0
RAID 0 has no redundancy.
RAID 6
Right. RAID 6 uses two parity blocks, so any two drives can fail.

q.q: What is the minimum number of drives for RAID 10?
o: Two drives is RAID 1 or RAID 0.
Six works, but it isn't the minimum.
Three drives is the minimum for RAID 5.
Right. RAID 10 is a stripe of mirrors, so it needs at least two mirrored pairs.

q.q: A video editing workstation needs the fastest scratch storage possible and the user accepts losing it if a drive fails. Which choice fits?
o: RAID 0 across two NVMe SSDs
Right. Striping splits data across drives for speed. There's no redundancy, which is acceptable for scratch space.
One 5,400 RPM hard drive
That's the slowest option listed.
RAID 1 across two 7,200 RPM HDDs
Mirroring protects data but doesn't add write speed, and HDDs are slow.
RAID 6 across four HDDs
RAID 6 protects data, but parity writes slow it down.

q.q: A new laptop image needs BitLocker to store its keys in hardware on the motherboard. Which component must be enabled in firmware?
o: Secure Boot
Secure Boot checks boot loader signatures. It doesn't store BitLocker keys.
Virtualization support
VT-x/AMD-V lets a CPU run VMs efficiently.
TPM
Right. The Trusted Platform Module stores encryption keys and supports measured boot.
An HSM card
A hardware security module is a separate high-end device, usually for servers.

q.q: A technician enables Secure Boot. What does it protect against?
o: Unsigned boot loaders and drivers
Right. Secure Boot only allows trusted, signed boot code to run at startup.
Stolen drives being read on another PC
That's what drive encryption protects against.
CPUs overheating when the fans fail at startup
Thermal protection handles overheating.
Weak Wi-Fi passwords
Secure Boot has nothing to do with Wi-Fi.

q.q: A user's VM software says the CPU doesn't support hardware virtualization, but the CPU's spec sheet says it does. What should the technician check?
o: That virtualization (VT-x or AMD-V) is enabled in UEFI/BIOS
Right. Hardware virtualization support is often off by default in firmware.
That the CPU is overclocked
Overclocking doesn't turn on virtualization.
That the PSU is modular
PSU design has nothing to do with virtualization.
That the RAM is ECC
ECC isn't required for VMs.

q.q: A small form factor PC case only fits a 17 x 17 cm motherboard. Which form factor should the technician buy?
o: microATX
microATX is about 24.4 x 24.4 cm.
Extended ATX
E-ATX is larger than ATX.
Mini-ITX
Right. Mini-ITX boards are 17 x 17 cm.
ATX
ATX is about 30.5 x 24.4 cm.

q.q: A PC needs a 10 GbE network card and a new GPU. Which expansion interface do both use?
o: PCIe
Right. Modern GPUs and NICs plug into PCIe slots of different lane widths.
M.2 SATA
M.2 SATA slots are for SSDs.
PCI
Legacy PCI is too slow and mostly gone from modern boards.
SATA
SATA connects drives.

q.q: A workstation's parts need about 520 W at full load. Which PSU is the best choice?
o: Two 300 W units wired in series
Standard PC PSUs aren't combined that way.
A 520 W unit sized exactly to the load
Running a PSU at 100% all the time is hard on it and leaves no headroom.
A 450 W 80 Plus unit
That's below the system's peak need, so it may shut down under load.
A 650 W 80 Plus unit
Right. Some headroom above peak load keeps the PSU cooler and more efficient.

q.q: A critical server must keep running if one power supply fails. What should it have?
o: A higher-wattage single PSU
One PSU is still a single point of failure.
A rack surge protector
A surge protector doesn't replace a failed PSU.
Redundant hot-swap PSUs
Right. Two PSUs share the load, and either can carry the server alone.
A fully modular, high-efficiency PSU
Modular just means detachable cables.

q.q: Which voltages does a standard ATX power supply provide to components?
o: 1.2 V and 1.35 V only
1.2 V is regulated on the motherboard for some parts, not supplied by the PSU.
3.3 V, 5 V and 12 V
Right. ATX PSUs supply 3.3, 5 and 12 V DC rails.
24 V and 48 V
Those aren't standard ATX rails.
120 V and 240 V
Those are AC input voltages from the wall.

q.q: Staff print sensitive evaluations to a shared office printer. Which feature keeps the pages from sitting in the tray?
o: A larger paper tray
Tray size doesn't protect printouts.
Secure print (PIN or badge release)
Right. The job is held until the user authenticates at the printer.
Duplex printing
Duplex prints on both sides.
Collation with a separator page per user
Collation orders multi-copy jobs.

q.q: A new network MFD should email scans to staff. Which settings must be configured on it?
o: The fuser temperature
The fuser affects print quality only.
The SMTP server, port and login
Right. Scan-to-email sends through an SMTP mail server.
The DHCP lease time and a DHCP reservation
The lease affects addressing, not email delivery.
The duplex unit
Duplex is for printing on both sides.

q.q: Which printer type uses heat on special paper and is common for receipts and shipping labels?
o: Thermal
Right. Direct thermal printers darken heat-sensitive paper. No ink or toner is needed.
Dot-matrix impact
Impact printers strike a ribbon, often for multipart forms.
Inkjet
Inkjets spray liquid ink.
Laser
Laser printers fuse toner.

q.q: A laser printer's page count passes the point the manufacturer lists for routine service. What should be installed?
o: A maintenance kit
Right. Maintenance kits (fuser and rollers) replace parts that wear on a schedule, then the page counter is reset.
A new print head
Laser printers don't have print heads.
A new ribbon
Ribbons are for impact printers.
Fresh thermal paper
Thermal paper is for thermal printers.

q.q: A thermal label printer is producing faint, streaky labels. What is the right first maintenance step?
o: Change the drum
Drums are in laser printers.
Replace the toner
Thermal printers don't use toner.
Clean the heating element with isopropyl alcohol
Right. Residue on the print head is a common cause of faint thermal prints.
Run an ink head alignment
Thermal printers have no ink.

q.q: An inkjet printer prints with missing lines and wrong colors after sitting unused for weeks. What should the technician do first?
o: Replace the fuser
Inkjets don't have fusers.
Run head cleaning and a nozzle check
Right. Dried ink clogs nozzles, and the built-in cleaning cycle usually clears them.
Install a laser maintenance kit
That kit is for laser printers.
Replace the impact ribbon and print head
Ribbons are for impact printers.

q.q: A data center server runs a hypervisor directly on the hardware with no host OS underneath. Which type is it?
o: A VDI client application on each PC
A VDI client connects to remote desktops.
A container engine
Containers share the host OS kernel. They aren't hypervisors.
Type 1 (bare metal)
Right. A Type 1 hypervisor runs directly on the hardware, like ESXi or Hyper-V Server.
Type 2 (hosted)
A Type 2 hypervisor runs as an app on a host OS, like VirtualBox on Windows.

q.q: A technician wants to test a suspicious email attachment without risking their real workstation. Which option fits best?
o: Open it on the workstation with antivirus off
That exposes the real system.
Open it in a sandbox VM and roll back after
Right. A sandbox VM keeps the file away from the host, and a snapshot can undo any changes.
Open it on a coworker's laptop
That moves the risk to someone else's real system.
Rename the file's extension to .txt and open it in Notepad
Renaming doesn't make malware safe.

q.q: Developers want to package an app with its libraries so it runs the same on every server, while sharing the host OS kernel. What should they use?
o: Type 1 VMs
VMs each run a full OS, which is heavier than a container.
A SAN
A SAN is storage.
VDI
VDI delivers desktops to users.
Containers
Right. Containers bundle an app and its dependencies, but share the host's kernel, so they're lighter than VMs.

q.q: A unit wants staff to use a standard Windows desktop that runs in the data center, reached from any thin client. What is this?
o: A Type 2 hypervisor on each PC
That runs VMs locally on each PC.
A container registry
A registry stores container images.
Virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI)
Right. VDI hosts desktops on central servers and streams them to clients.
SaaS email
SaaS delivers one app, not a full desktop.

q.q: A technician wants to run three VMs on a laptop at the same time. Which resource is most likely to run out first?
o: RAM
Right. Every running VM needs its own RAM set aside, so memory runs out fastest.
The USB ports
VMs don't need their own USB ports.
The Wi-Fi channel
VMs share the host's network connection.
The screen resolution
Resolution doesn't limit VM count.

q.q: Why should VMs get the same patching and security as physical machines?
o: VMs are always isolated from the network and from each other
Most VMs are connected to networks.
Patching VMs is required only for licensing
Patching is about security, not licensing.
VMs can't be infected by malware
VMs run real operating systems, so they can be infected.
VMs can be compromised, and an escape could reach the host
Right. Guest OSes have the same vulnerabilities, and a flaw in the hypervisor could let an attacker out.

q.q: Which TWO statements about Type 2 hypervisors are true? (Choose two.)
o: They run directly on bare metal with no host OS
That describes Type 1.
They don't need any CPU virtualization support
Modern hypervisors rely on VT-x or AMD-V for good performance.
They run as an application on top of a host operating system
Right. VirtualBox and VMware Workstation run on Windows, macOS or Linux.
They're common for testing and training on desktops and laptops
Right. They're easy to install on a normal PC.
They give better performance than Type 1 for data centers
The extra host OS layer usually makes them slower.

q.q: A unit rents virtual servers in the cloud and manages the OS, patches and apps itself. Which service model is this?
o: IaaS
Right. With infrastructure as a service, the provider runs hardware and virtualization. The customer manages the OS and up.
On-premises
On-premises hardware is owned and run in-house.
SaaS
With SaaS, the provider runs everything, including the app.
PaaS
With PaaS, the provider also manages the OS and runtime.

q.q: Staff use web-based email and documents. The provider handles all servers, updates and the app. Which model is this?
o: PaaS
PaaS gives developers a platform to deploy their own code.
IaaS
With IaaS, the customer manages the OS and apps.
A private cloud
That's a deployment model, not a service model.
SaaS
Right. Software as a service delivers a finished app. The customer just uses it.

q.q: Developers want to upload their code and have the provider handle the OS, runtime and scaling. Which model fits?
o: SaaS
SaaS is a finished app for end users.
A hybrid cloud
That's a deployment model.
IaaS
With IaaS, developers would manage the OS themselves.
PaaS
Right. Platform as a service manages the OS and runtime so developers can focus on code.

q.q: A cloud app adds servers automatically during a surge in traffic and removes them afterward. Which characteristic is this?
o: File synchronization
File sync keeps files the same across devices.
Metered utilization
Metering means paying for what you use.
Rapid elasticity
Right. Elasticity scales resources up and down with demand.
Multitenancy across customers
Multitenancy means many customers share the same infrastructure.

q.q: A unit keeps sensitive records in its own data center but bursts extra work into a public cloud during busy periods. Which deployment model is this?
o: Public cloud only
That would put everything with the provider.
Hybrid cloud
Right. A hybrid cloud combines private and public cloud resources.
Private cloud
That would keep everything in-house.
Community cloud
A community cloud is shared by organizations with common needs.

q.q: The unit's cloud bill rises and falls each month with how much storage and compute it actually used. Which characteristic is this?
o: Rapid elasticity
Elasticity is the scaling itself, not how it's billed.
Metered utilization
Right. Cloud providers meter usage and bill for what is consumed.
Shared, pooled resources across tenants
Shared resources describe pooled hardware.
High availability
High availability is about uptime, not billing.

q.q: Several agencies with the same compliance needs share one cloud built just for them. Which deployment model is this?
o: Public cloud
A public cloud is open to any customer.
Private cloud
A private cloud serves one organization.
Community cloud
Right. A community cloud serves several organizations that share requirements.
Hybrid cloud with a VPN link
Hybrid mixes private and public.

q.q: A desktop resets its date and time to 2010 every time it's unplugged overnight. What is the most likely fix?
o: Replace the CMOS battery
Right. The coin cell keeps firmware settings and the clock when the PC has no power.
Reinstall the operating system
The clock resets before the OS loads.
Reseat the RAM
RAM doesn't hold the system clock.
Replace the power supply
The PC runs normally when plugged in, so the PSU works.

q.q: A workstation shuts off without warning after about 20 minutes of heavy use, and the case feels hot. What should the technician check first?
o: The monitor cable
A bad cable affects the picture, not system power.
The Wi-Fi card and its antenna leads
The Wi-Fi card doesn't cause thermal shutdowns.
The keyboard drivers
Drivers don't make a hot PC shut off.
Cooling: fans, heat sink, paste and dust
Right. Random shutdowns under load with heat point to overheating, which triggers thermal protection.

q.q: A PC powers on, fans spin, but there's no video and it gives a repeating beep pattern. What does this most likely point to?
o: A failed hard drive or a missing boot partition
A missing drive gives a boot device message after POST, not usually a beep code.
An expired software license
Licensing has nothing to do with POST.
A corrupt OS installation
The OS hasn't loaded yet when POST fails.
A POST failure (often RAM or video)
Right. Beep codes report POST failures. Check the board maker's beep code chart.

q.q: A technician notices bulging, leaking capacitors near the CPU socket of an old PC that reboots at random. What is the right action?
o: Reset the BIOS to defaults
Settings can't repair physical damage.
Update the OS
Software can't fix failing hardware.
Replace the motherboard
Right. Swollen capacitors mean the board is failing, and repair isn't practical.
Add more RAM
More RAM doesn't fix bad capacitors.

q.q: A PC smells like something is burning and shuts off. What should the technician do first?
o: Run a full antivirus scan
Malware doesn't cause a burning smell.
Defragment the hard drive and clear the temp files
Defragmenting doesn't fix overheating parts.
Power it off and unplug it, then inspect
Right. A burning smell means a component is overheating or failing. Remove power first for safety.
Keep using it to see if the smell goes away
That risks fire and more damage.

q.q: A PC gets frequent blue screens that name different drivers each time. Memory diagnostics report errors. What is the most likely cause?
o: A full hard drive
A full drive slows a PC but doesn't fail memory tests.
A bad keyboard
A keyboard doesn't cause memory test failures.
A weak Wi-Fi signal
Wi-Fi problems cause slow networking, not memory errors.
Faulty RAM
Right. Random crashes with varied errors plus failed memory tests point to bad RAM.

q.q: A desktop has no lights, fans or sound when the power button is pressed. The outlet works. What should the technician check?
o: The boot order in the UEFI settings
Boot order matters only once the PC powers up.
The PSU switch, cable and the PSU
Right. With no signs of life at all, check that power is getting into and out of the PSU.
The monitor's input source
The PC itself shows no life, so the monitor isn't the issue.
The CMOS battery
A dead CMOS battery resets settings. It doesn't stop the PC from powering on.

q.q: A user's laptop makes a clicking noise and files take a long time to open. S.M.A.R.T. reports a predicted failure. What should the technician do first?
o: Run defragmentation
Heavy reads and writes on a failing drive can finish it off.
Increase virtual memory
That adds more load on a failing drive.
Reinstall the OS
The drive is the problem, not the OS.
Back up the data right away, then replace the drive
Right. Clicking and a S.M.A.R.T. warning mean the drive could fail any time. Save the data first.

q.q: A PC shows "bootable device not found" after a technician installed a second drive. What is the most likely cause?
o: The CPU wasn't reseated after the drive install
A loose CPU gives no POST.
Boot order now points at the empty drive
Right. Firmware may try to boot from the newly added drive. Set the OS drive first.
The monitor cable is loose
The error message is showing, so video works.
The RAM failed during the install
RAM failure usually gives beep codes or crashes.

q.q: A RAID 5 array with four drives reports one failed drive, but the server is still running. What should the technician do?
o: Replace the failed drive so it can rebuild
Right. RAID 5 runs degraded after one failure. A second failure before the rebuild would lose the data.
Nothing, since RAID 5 can lose any number of drives
RAID 5 survives only one failure.
Remove a second drive to balance it
That would destroy the array.
Convert it to RAID 0 for more space
RAID 0 has no redundancy and the data would be lost.

q.q: A technician hears grinding from a hard drive in an old PC. What does this point to?
o: A disk that is almost full of data
A full disk doesn't make mechanical noise.
A loose SATA data cable
A loose cable causes detection errors, not grinding.
Mechanical failure in the drive
Right. Grinding often means the heads are touching the platters. The drive is failing.
A low CMOS battery
That causes clock resets.

q.q: A RAID 1 mirror shows both drives online, but one drive's data is out of date after a power loss. What should happen?
o: Convert to RAID 0
RAID 0 removes protection.
Rebuild the mirror from the healthy, current drive
Right. The controller copies the good drive onto the stale one to resync the mirror.
Ignore it, since mirrors fix themselves after a reboot
Some controllers resync automatically, but it has to be confirmed, not assumed.
Format both drives
That would erase the good data too.

q.q: A laptop screen is very dim, but the image is visible with a flashlight shined on it. What has most likely failed?
o: The GPU
A failed GPU would give no image at all.
The backlight (or its inverter on older CCFL models)
Right. A faint image you can see with outside light means the panel works but its light source doesn't.
The display driver
A driver problem usually affects resolution or causes artifacts, not a dim image you can still see.
The digitizer
The digitizer handles touch, not brightness.

q.q: A conference room projector shuts off by itself after about 15 minutes. What should the technician check first?
o: Its air filter and fans (overheating)
Right. Projectors protect themselves by shutting down when they get too hot.
The laptop's display settings
Laptop settings don't turn off the projector.
The HDMI cable
A bad cable causes no signal, not a full shutdown.
The projection screen's surface and mounting
The screen doesn't affect the projector.

q.q: A watch-center monitor that shows the same map all day now keeps a faint ghost image of it even after the map closes. What is this?
o: A loose video cable
A loose cable causes flicker or no signal.
Burn-in
Right. A static image shown for a long time can leave a lasting ghost, especially on OLED.
Dead pixels
Dead pixels are single dots that stay black or one color.
Incorrect color depth
Color depth affects how many colors show.

q.q: After a driver update, a monitor shows a fuzzy, stretched image. What should the technician check first?
o: The monitor's power cable
Power problems cause no image, not fuzziness.
That it's set to the native resolution
Right. LCDs look sharp only at their native resolution.
The CMOS battery
The CMOS battery doesn't affect display scaling.
The projector bulb and the monitor's power-saving mode
This is a monitor, not a projector.

q.q: Users see a monitor flicker on and off. Moving the cable at the back makes it worse. What is the most likely cause?
o: A full hard drive
Storage space doesn't affect video signal.
A loose or damaged video cable
Right. If moving the cable changes the problem, the connection is faulty.
Burn-in
Burn-in is a ghost image, not flicker.
The wrong refresh rate in the OS
That wouldn't change when the cable moves.

q.q: A phone's battery health is at 72% and it dies by mid-afternoon. What is the best fix?
o: Turn on 5G only to save power
5G can use more power, not less.
Charge it to 100% overnight every night
Charging habits don't bring back lost capacity.
Factory reset the phone
A reset doesn't restore battery capacity.
Replace the battery
Right. Lithium-ion batteries lose capacity with age. A worn battery has to be replaced.

q.q: A phone dropped in seawater still turns on. What should the user do?
o: Dry it with a hair dryer on high heat
High heat can damage the battery and screen.
Charge it to make sure it still works
Charging a wet phone can short it.
Power it off now and get it serviced
Right. Salt water corrodes circuits fast. Powering it off cuts the risk of shorts.
Put it in rice and keep using it
Rice doesn't remove corrosion, and using it risks shorts.

q.q: A tablet gets hot and the battery drains fast even when it's idle. What should the technician check first?
o: The Bluetooth pairing list
Paired devices don't usually cause heavy drain.
The SIM card and carrier settings
The SIM card doesn't cause heat.
The screen's digitizer
Touch problems don't cause heat.
Battery usage for a runaway app
Right. A background app using CPU all the time causes heat and drain.

q.q: A phone can't connect to any Bluetooth device, even after restarts. Other wireless works. What should the technician try?
o: Remove the SIM
The SIM doesn't control Bluetooth.
Reset network settings
Right. Resetting network settings clears corrupt Bluetooth and Wi-Fi settings without erasing user data.
Replace the battery
Battery health doesn't stop Bluetooth.
Lower the screen brightness
Brightness doesn't affect Bluetooth.

q.q: A phone screen responds to touch in some areas but not others after it was dropped. The glass isn't cracked. What has most likely failed?
o: The Wi-Fi radio
Wi-Fi doesn't control touch.
The speaker
The speaker is for sound.
The digitizer
Right. The touch layer can be damaged even when the glass looks fine.
The battery
Battery problems affect power, not touch zones.

q.q: A user's wireless connection drops every few minutes, but only when the break room microwave runs. What is the cause?
o: An expired DHCP lease
That wouldn't line up with the microwave.
2.4 GHz interference
Right. Microwave ovens give off energy near 2.4 GHz. Moving the user to 5 GHz avoids it.
A wrong DNS server on the laptop
DNS problems don't cause the link to drop.
A bad Ethernet cable at the desk
The user is on wireless.

q.q: VoIP calls sound choppy, and network tests show the delay between packets varies widely. What is this problem called?
o: APIPA addressing
APIPA is a fallback IP address.
Jitter
Right. Jitter is uneven delay between packets. It hurts voice and video quality.
Crosstalk
Crosstalk is signal bleeding between wire pairs.
Port flapping
Port flapping is a switch port going up and down.

q.q: A switch log shows one port going up and down many times a minute. What is this called, and what is a common cause?
o: Burn-in, from a static image
Burn-in is a display issue.
Port flapping, often from a bad cable or NIC
Right. A port that keeps changing state usually has a physical problem on the link.
APIPA, from a DHCP outage
APIPA is an address, not a port problem.
Jitter, from too many users
Jitter is about packet timing, not port state.

q.q: A laptop connected to Wi-Fi shows "No internet," and its address is 169.254.18.7. What should the technician check?
o: Whether the DHCP server is reachable
Right. 169.254.x.x is APIPA, which means the laptop got no DHCP reply.
The laptop's RAID array and drive health
Storage doesn't affect addressing.
The laptop's screen resolution
Display settings don't affect addressing.
The printer's toner
The printer isn't involved.

q.q: Users on one floor have slow internet, but local file transfers are fast. What should the technician check?
o: Each user's monitor cable
Video cables don't affect network speed.
The printers and print queues on that floor
Printers don't slow internet access.
The internet link, firewall and router
Right. Fast local traffic means the LAN is fine. The slowdown is on the path out.
The CMOS battery on each PC
That affects the clock.

q.q: A laser printer's pages come out with toner that smears off when rubbed. Which part has most likely failed?
o: The pickup roller
The pickup roller feeds paper.
The network card
The network card doesn't affect print quality.
The transfer belt
The transfer belt moves toner to the paper but doesn't bond it.
The fuser
Right. The fuser melts toner onto the paper. If it fails, toner sits loose on the page.

q.q: A laser printer puts the same vertical black line down every page. What is the most likely cause?
o: A wrong paper size setting
That causes cropping or a paper error.
A scratched drum
Right. A scratch or debris on the drum repeats in the same spot on every page.
A failed fuser
A bad fuser causes smearing, not a sharp line.
A low battery
Printers aren't battery-powered.

q.q: A laser printer shows a faint copy of the image a few inches lower on the page. What is this called, and what is a common cause?
o: Garbled print, from a driver problem
Garbled print is wrong characters.
Speckling, from loose toner
Speckling is random dots.
A paper jam, from a bad tray
Jams stop the paper.
Ghosting, often from a worn drum or fuser
Right. Leftover toner or charge prints a second, faint copy of the image.

q.q: A printer prints pages of random symbols for every job from one PC. Other PCs print fine. What should the technician check?
o: The building's power
Power doesn't cause symbols from one PC only.
The printer's toner
Toner problems affect every job.
That PC's print driver
Right. Garbled output from one PC points to a wrong or corrupt driver on that PC.
The printer's fuser
A fuser problem would affect every PC.

q.q: A laser printer keeps jamming, and it often pulls several sheets at once. What should the technician check first?
o: The print driver on the server
Drivers don't control how paper is picked up.
The pickup rollers
Right. Worn pickup and separation rollers lose grip and either miss sheets or pull several together.
The network cable and the printer's IP settings
Cables don't affect paper feeding.
The toner cartridge
Toner affects the image, not feeding.

q.title: Build the network for a small recruiting office
q.scenario: A recruiting office has a new fiber internet service. The provider's fiber cable ends at a wall box in the closet. Staff laptops use Wi-Fi from ONE access point cabled back to the closet, and a camera watches the front door. Neither the access point nor the camera has a power adapter, and no outlets are near them. Place each device. Some in the tray are not needed.
q.ticket: Install work order 2291: fiber service, one closet, two cable runs (ceiling and front door).

devs.name: Optical network terminal
devs.why: Fiber carries light, not Ethernet. The optical network terminal (ONT) turns the light signal into a normal Ethernet connection for the router.

devs.name: SOHO router with firewall
devs.why: The router does network address translation (NAT), which lets all the inside devices share one public address. Its firewall blocks unwanted traffic from the Internet.

devs.name: PoE switch
devs.why: A Power over Ethernet (PoE) switch sends power down the same cable as the data. That is how the access point and the camera run with no adapters and no outlets.

devs.name: Wireless access point
devs.why: The access point gives laptops Wi-Fi and is cabled to the switch, which also powers it. It belongs in the ceiling for even coverage.

devs.name: PoE IP camera
devs.why: An IP camera sends video over the network. A PoE model takes its power from the same cable, so it can sit at the front door.

devs.name: Cable modem
devs.why: A cable modem is for a cable TV (coax) provider. This service is fiber, so the optical network terminal is the right device.

devs.name: Wireless range extender
devs.why: An extender repeats Wi-Fi over the air and often cuts the speed. Here a cable already reaches the ceiling, so an access point on that cable is the better choice.

devs.name: Ethernet hub
devs.why: A hub repeats every frame out of every port, shares the bandwidth and cannot power devices. A PoE switch does all the needed work better.

devs.name: Single-port PoE injector
devs.why: An injector powers only one device. It could not serve as the closet switch that connects the router, the access point and the camera together.

q.title: A wired PC can reach servers by number but not by name

checks.why: The settings list shows this PC uses a fixed address, and its DNS server is 10.20.9.9. Reading them first shows what the PC is told to use.
A reply from the gateway shows the cable, the switch port and the PC's address all work on the local network.

checks.t: Proved the Internet answers by number
checks.why: A reply from an outside address, with no name used, shows routing and the gateway are fine. That narrows the fault to turning names into addresses.

checks.t: Saw the name lookup time out
checks.why: nslookup asks a DNS server for a name. A timeout from 10.20.9.9 shows that server is the one that does not answer.

checks.t: Asked the unit DNS server directly
checks.why: The correct server at 10.20.0.2 answers right away. That shows the DNS service is healthy and this PC is pointed at the wrong one.
The fault is only the DNS server setting. Changing it to the unit's server fixes the cause.

checks.t: Did not reset the whole network stack
checks.why: netsh int ip reset rewrites the TCP/IP settings and can wipe the static address. netsh winsock reset rebuilds the network socket catalog. Both need a restart, and one wrong DNS entry calls for neither.

checks.t: Showed the name resolves after the fix
checks.why: Always test the real symptom again. The intranet name now resolves and answers a ping.

q.title: Read the file server's RAID and drive log
q.scenario: The records file server nas01 sends this morning's log to the help desk. Its storage is a RAID 5 array, which spreads data and parity (extra recovery data) over four drives so one drive can fail without data loss. Mark the lines that point to the problem and leave the normal ones alone. Then pick what the technician should do.
q.ticket: Ticket 6102: nas01 console shows a drive warning icon. Array status: Optimal.

lines.text: Nov 24 01:50:02 nas01 raid: inventory: VD0 RAID 5, 4 drives; bay 2 = /dev/sdc
lines.why: A routine inventory line. It only tells you which drive sits in which bay.

lines.text: Nov 24 02:00:04 nas01 raid: scheduled consistency check started on VD0
lines.why: A scheduled check reads the array to make sure the data and parity agree. Starting it is normal.

lines.text: Nov 24 02:41:17 nas01 raid: PD2 (bay 2) media error at LBA 0x1A2B3C, corrected by retry
lines.why: A media error means the drive had trouble reading a spot on its disk. A retry fixed this one, but it is the first sign of trouble on bay 2.

lines.text: Nov 24 02:58:30 nas01 smartd: /dev/sdc SMART Attribute 5 Reallocated_Sector_Ct raw=64 (was 0 last week)
lines.why: The drive moved 64 bad sectors to spare ones in a week. This count comes from S.M.A.R.T. (Self-Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Technology), the drive's built-in health check. A fast rise is a classic sign of a dying drive.

lines.text: Nov 24 03:12:09 nas01 raid: PD0 (bay 0) temperature 38 C, normal
lines.why: A cool drive in a different bay. It is normal and not part of the fault.

lines.text: Nov 24 03:30:55 nas01 smartd: /dev/sda SMART overall health: PASSED
lines.why: A healthy report for a different drive. Only bay 2 is showing trouble.

lines.text: Nov 24 04:05:02 nas01 raid: PD2 (bay 2) media error at LBA 0x1A2B9F, retry failed, sector remapped
lines.why: This time the retry failed. The same drive is hitting more bad spots, so the problem is growing.

lines.text: Nov 24 04:20:44 nas01 smartd: /dev/sdc SMART Attribute 197 Current_Pending_Sector raw=12
lines.why: Pending sectors are spots the drive cannot read and is waiting to remap. Twelve of them, on the same drive, back up the other lines.

lines.text: Nov 24 05:00:01 nas01 backup: nightly job to usb-vault finished, 412 GB, 0 errors
lines.why: A good backup with no errors. It is useful to know, but it is not a fault.

lines.text: Nov 24 05:10:33 nas01 raid: PD2 (bay 2) command timeout, drive reset by controller
lines.why: The drive stopped answering and the controller had to reset it. Timeouts on top of media errors point to a failing drive.

lines.text: Nov 24 05:11:02 nas01 raid: VD0 state Optimal, consistency check 62% complete
lines.why: The array is still healthy, with parity protecting the data. This is not a fault, but it also is not a reason to wait.

lines.text: Nov 24 06:30:00 nas01 ntpd: time synchronized with ntp.unit.example
lines.why: A normal time sync. Unrelated to the drive.

lines.text: Nov 24 07:15:20 nas01 raid: PD1 (bay 1) patrol read completed, 0 errors
lines.why: A clean read of a different drive. It shows the other bays are fine.

ask.label: What should the technician do?
opts: Replace the RAID controller, since it had to reset a drive
Replace the bay 2 drive soon, after checking the backup is good
Wait for the consistency check to finish, since it repairs bad sectors
Pull the bay 2 drive now; the array is Optimal, so no backup check is needed
ask.why: Every warning points to one drive, bay 2, and it is getting worse. RAID 5 survives one failed drive, so replace this one before a second drive fails. Confirm the backup first, because a rebuild reads every other drive hard, and an Optimal status does not replace a backup. The controller only reset the one drive that stopped answering, and bays 0 and 1 and /dev/sda look healthy. A check cannot repair a drive that is wearing out. Rebuilding the whole array is far more work than one swap.

q.title: Set up a unit phone for a deploying member
q.scenario: A new unit-issued phone is going to a member who will deploy. The unit needs work email, contacts and calendar on the phone. IT must be able to lock or wipe it if it is lost. The phone's cellular plan has a 5 GB monthly data cap, so photo backups must not use it. Build the steps in the order you would do them. Leave out steps that do not belong.
q.ticket: Request MD-0417: new phone for a deploying member, 5 GB monthly data cap.

rules.text: Enroll the phone in the unit's mobile device management (MDM)
rules.why: MDM is software that lets IT push settings and lock or wipe a phone from a console. Enrolling is what gives IT remote wipe if the phone is lost.

rules.text: Set a PIN screen lock that meets the MDM policy
rules.why: A screen lock keeps a stranger out of mail and contacts. It is also a common MDM compliance rule, and a lock helps protect data on a lost phone.

rules.text: Add the unit email account so mail, contacts and calendar sync
rules.why: Adding the account sets up a two-way sync with the server. Do it after enrollment, so the policy rules already protect the data when it arrives.

rules.text: Set photo backup to upload on Wi-Fi only
rules.why: Backups over cellular would eat the 5 GB cap. A Wi-Fi only setting uploads when the phone is on a network with no data cap.

rules.text: Send a test email and check the MDM console shows the phone compliant
rules.why: A last check proves mail syncs and that IT can see and manage the phone. Do not hand a phone over without it.

rules.text: Set app and photo updates to use cellular data so they finish faster
rules.why: Updates and uploads over cellular spend the 5 GB cap. Wi-Fi only keeps the data plan for real use.

rules.text: Set up the email account with POP3
rules.why: POP3 downloads mail to one device and can remove it from the server. It does not sync contacts or calendar, and neither does IMAP. A work account that uses Exchange ActiveSync (or Microsoft 365) syncs all three.

rules.text: Turn off location services so the member cannot be tracked
rules.why: MDM uses the phone's location to help find a lost phone. Turning it off weakens the lock and wipe plan.

rules.text: Turn on a permanent mobile hotspot for the team
rules.why: A hotspot shares the member's cellular data, which has a small cap. It also opens another way into the phone.

before.why: Enroll first so the unit's rules cover the phone before any work data arrives.

last.why: The test only means something once everything else is set up.

q.title: Open a suspicious file safely in a virtual machine
q.scenario: A user forwarded a file that may be harmful. With written approval from your supervisor, you will open it in a virtual machine (VM) on your lab host. A snapshot saves a VM's state so you can go back to it later. The file must not reach the real network or your host. Build the steps in order. Leave out steps that put the host or network at risk.
q.ticket: Work order VM-218: authorized test of one forwarded file on the lab host.

rules.text: Create the VM and install a clean guest OS
rules.why: The VM is a separate computer made in software. A fresh guest operating system gives a known clean base.

rules.text: Disconnect the VM's virtual network adapter
rules.why: With no network adapter the file cannot reach the real network or the host, so it cannot spread or call out to an attacker.

rules.text: Take a snapshot of the clean, isolated VM
rules.why: The snapshot is the point to go back to. Take it before the file is opened, or there is nothing clean to return to.

rules.text: Attach a disc image (ISO) holding the file, then open it inside the VM
rules.why: A disc image is read-only, so it moves the file into the VM without opening a path back to the host. The file then runs only inside the VM, after the VM is isolated and saved.

rules.text: Revert the VM to the clean snapshot when finished
rules.why: Reverting throws away every change the file made, so the next test starts clean.

rules.text: Use bridged networking so the VM can fetch updates
rules.why: Bridged mode puts the VM on the real network as its own device. A harmful file could then reach other computers.

rules.text: Turn on shared folders and drag-and-drop with the host
rules.why: These features make a path between the VM and the host. Harmful files can use that path to reach the host's files.

rules.text: Use NAT networking so the VM hides behind the host
rules.why: NAT still lets the VM reach the network through the host, so a harmful file could call out or spread.

rules.text: Delete the snapshot after opening the file to save disk space
rules.why: Deleting it removes the clean point to return to, and the VM would stay changed.

rules.text: Set the VM's network to host-only so it can only reach the lab host
rules.why: Host-only still links the VM to the host, which this test must protect.

before.why: The snapshot saves the installed system, so the install comes first.
Cut the network connection before the file is opened, or it could reach out the moment it runs.
Take the snapshot before opening the file, so it holds the clean state.

last.why: Revert once the testing is done.
